knowledge_point.title: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With the Tangent Trigonometric Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ Applying these formulas, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}+tan⁡x) \\  & =1\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})+1\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})+1({sec}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{\sqrt{x}}+{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The instantaneous rate of change  when $x=\pi$ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=\pi .$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-tan⁡x) \\  & =-{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\pi ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-{sec}^{2}⁡\pi  \\  & =-1\cdot (-1)^{2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The instantaneous rate of change when $x=0$ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=0.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x$ and $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})=2x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{tan}⁡x-{x}^{2}) \\  & =4{sec}^{2}⁡x-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0) & =4{sec}^{2}⁡(0)-2\cdot 0 \\  & =4{(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)})}^{2}-0 \\  & =4{(\frac{1}{1})}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is $4.$

\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(0)+cos⁡(0) \\  & =1+1(1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x.$ Applying the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(6 x - 2 \tan x\right) \\ &= -2\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\tan x\right) + 6\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x\right) \\ &= 6 - 2 \sec^{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=- \frac{\pi}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y'(- \frac{\pi}{4})&=6 - 2 \sec^{2}\left(- \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ &= 2 \\ &= 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope is $2.$

We know that $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x.$ Applying the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(3 x^{2} + 2 \sin x - 6 \cos x + 2 \tan x\right) \\ &= -6\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\cos x\right) + 2\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\sin x\right) + 2\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\tan x\right) + 3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{2}\right) \\ &= 6 x + 6 \sin x + 2 \cos x + 2 \sec^{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x.$ Applying the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(2 x^{2} + 3 \sin x - 3 \cos x + 3 \tan x\right) \\ &= -3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\cos x\right) + 2\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{2}\right) + 3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\sin x\right) + 3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\tan x\right) \\ &= 4 x + 3 \sin x + 3 \cos x + 3 \sec^{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x.$ Applying the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(3 x^{4} + 9 \sin x - 3 \cos x + 3 \tan x\right) \\ &= -3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\cos x\right) + 3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{4}\right) + 3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\tan x\right) + 9\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\sin x\right) \\ &= 12 x^{3} + 3 \sin x + 9 \cos x + 3 \sec^{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x.$ Applying the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(2 x^{4} + 8 \sin x - 8 \cos x + 4 \tan x\right) \\ &= -8\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\cos x\right) + 2\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{4}\right) + 4\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\tan x\right) + 8\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\sin x\right) \\ &= 8 x^{3} + 8 \sin x + 8 \cos x + 4 \sec^{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$
